note: Zimbabwe, read on the Department of Immigration's Permits and Fees pages (zimimmigration.gov.zw) and in the Immigration Act (Chapter 4:02) as it serves it, on 2026-10-30; fees are set in US dollars, so the file's currency is USD. A temporary employment permit (the Act provides for it by regulation, s. 19) is asked on the residence permit form I.F.5 and the temporary employment application form, with a letter to the Chief Director of Immigration, the contract of employment, the post's local newspaper advertisement and the understudies' details; its statutory non-refundable fee is US$500 (US$300 per dependant; the fee page also lists a short term permit among temporary employment permit applicants at US$500), and an extension is asked with a copy of the current permit for US$500 (renewable). The pages don't say whether it is lodged from abroad or in Zimbabwe, nor whether the work it allows is bound to the employer, so where to apply and work are left out (an earlier draft read both in and was held). A non-investor's permanent residence permit costs US$500 (an investor's US$1,000); the pages don't say where it is asked, what work it allows or after how many years (the Act's domicile, ten years' lawful ordinary residence, excludes years on any permit other than a residence permit, so a temporary employment permit's years aren't read as leading to it). Terms and decision times aren't stated; naturalisation (the Citizenship of Zimbabwe Act) isn't written.
